raw_comment: In observing the graphs, I noticed that as time progressed into the later part of the 20th century, heavier precipitation occurred. From the 1901-1930 graph, precipitation seems to have a concentration in the southwest plains area of the US. The overall least amount of precipitation seems to occur in the 1931-1960 graph. Then in the 1961-1990 graph, the occurrence of precipitation is wide spread, but not in high concentration. However, the 1991-2021 graph shows high concentration of precipitation in the Northwest and Midwest - this being the largest span covered so far. I wonder if this increase of precipitation has something to do with factors such as climate change, or the occurrence of natural disasters such as tornadoes or hurricanes due to geographical location. This increase relates to me and my community because I live in the Northeast's high concentration. This could be harmful to habitats and organisms but also increase the viability of certain organisms. The graph is depicting the United States' levels of precipitation in 30 year increments from 1901-2021. "Recent Precipitation Levels are Raining on the US's Parade"

raw_comment: Observing the graphs, I noticed the high concentration of precipitation during the period of 1991-2021 in the Northeast area of the country and a pretty low concentration of precipitation in the western area. During the time of 1931-1960, I noticed that there is the least amount of precipitation shown in the graph than there is in any other time period. The precipitation in 1901-1930 and 1961-1990, is more equally distributed in the areas rather than one heavier than the other. I wonder why some areas receive more precipitation in comparison to others and why precipitation has increased so much during the more current years. This relates to me and my community because in the more recent times, precipitation has been heavy in the northeast, which is where I live. This increase in precipitation can be harmful to some organisms by destroying their habitats or causing them to make changes to their lifestyles. It can also be beneficial because it reduces the amount of droughts and water shortages. The graph shows the amount of precipitation across America from 1901-2020, distributed by 30 year increments. The headline I would make for this graph is, "Precipitation in America: How Much is it Changing?"

raw_comment: When I analyzed the precipitation graphs, I noticed that there is a heavy dry concentration in the western states during the 1931-1960 period, and that for the northwestern group, their precipitation does not keep a significant pattern throughout the 120 year time period. I also noticed that in the most recent observed time period, the precipitation in the northeastern states is the most extreme it has ever been since being observed. After looking through the graph and information, I now wonder why the precipitation has had such extreme measures in the past few years and if there are any factors that may have caused it to be that way. These graphs relate to my location; I live in the northeast and I have observed in my past 16 years of living here that a lot of rain has been the standard weather for spring and fall months especially. This drastic change of precipitation has the ability to increase biodiversity in my area and in the northeast as a whole, which can be beneficial. In this graph, precipitation levels are being recorded and the extremity of the level correlates to a certain color on the map. I would make the headline of this graph "Why is it Raining So Much? raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that from 1901 to 1930, the relative precipitation is pretty evenly spread across the US. From 1931 to 1960, the relative precipitation is very low, with the most dry areas being around the Midwest and the Southwest. From 1961 to 1990, the relative precipitation is also pretty evenly spread, with maybe a bit more precipitation overall. From 1991 to 2020, the relative precipitation is very high, with most of it concentrated in the Northeast and the Midwest.

What do you wonder?
I wonder why the precipitation levels fluctuate so much across the US?

How does this relate to you and your community?
Ever since I was born, I've noticed that it very rarely rains in Arizona, and I always wondered if Arizona was always like this. This data shows that Arizona wasn't always like this. Across the four time spans given in the graph, Arizona changes from having above average precipitation between 1901 and 1930, to having below average precipitation between 1931 and 1960, to having above average precipitation between 1961 and 1990, to having below average precipitation.

What’s going on in this graph? Create a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
This graph shows that America's overall precipitation has gone from average, to low, back to average again, and finally to high. My headline would be "Precipitation across the nation".

raw_comment:
The levels of precipitation have changed drastically in the last century as shown. The dry period in the western portion of the united states was at its worst point around 1930 but then in the 1990s to 2000 is the area with the most precipitation. The distribution among the graphs is interesting as it is not consistent in anyway, the areas that were dry have had periods of time with high precipitation and vice versa.

I wonder if the main cause of the large change in precipitation is climate change? If they conducted another study or mapped a prediction of the next 30 years, if the maps would show another drastic change where it is either a lot of precipitation or none? What has these changes in precipitation caused damage to in occupations like farming?

In New England experiencing random weather unexpectedly isn't a new thing, but the large changes in inches of snow or rain and really dry summers effect small things in the community like snow days for school. Other things that are effected are athletics and extra curriculars, even town events held outdoors. The weather also effects the United States community of nature and farming for food.

raw_comment:
HEADLINE: Is it still the government making things up? or is it really are thanks to global warning?
What do you notice?
This graph shows overall how the precipitation has affected USA during this last century
What do you wonder?
I wonder if maybe climate change may have been one of the main factor involving this change on the country
How does this relate to you and your community?
It doesn't affect my community but since we are part of the world, it is in my opinion that it affects all of us as a planet because it can cause the place we live in to have random rains or drought.

Is it still the government making things up?

This graph shows overall how the precipitation has affected USA during this last century.

It does not affect my community.

raw_comment:
I notice from this data that the levels of precipitation have dramatically increased on the Eastern side of the country, making it have a more wet climate, while the Southwest, in contrast, has become more of a dry environment throughout the years. Thus, from 1901-60, most of the West and East seemed to have a drier climate than from 1961-2020, which shows the transition into the wet environment in the majority of the East.
I wonder whether global warming is a factor in this change in the climate. The warmer the air is, the higher the humidity and quicker evaporation of water which prompts tropical storms and hurricanes that have been occurring more lately. Another factor that may play into this is geography. For example, a state such as Arizona, with its canyons and deserts, already contains a dry climate, and global warming elevates that climate.

raw_comment: I noticed as time passed, the amount of rainfall has significantly increased throughout almost the whole US. However, through time we also realize how the east side of the US has become much more humid as the west side loses its humidity. And for some reason, Arizona has become the driest and hottest state in the US. I wonder if climate change caused all these changes because of the knowledge that Texas has been one of the most affected states in the US (the snow incident). I also wouldn't say the development of the cities is a huge factor in these changes.

The east side of the US has become much more humid.
The west side loses its humidity.
Arizona has become the driest state in the US.
Arizona has become the hottest state in the US.
Climate change may have caused all these changes.
Texas has been one of the most affected states in the US.

Thus, from 1901-60, most of the West and East seemed to have a drier climate than from 1961-2020, which shows the transition into the wet environment in the majority of the East.
I wonder whether global warming is a factor in this change in the climate. Another factor that may play into this is the geography. For example, a state such as Arizona, with its canyons and deserts, already contain a dry climate, and global warming elevates that climate.

Title: "The Fall and Rise of Rainfall"

I noticed that over time, the areas that used to have more precipitation now have less, and the areas that used to have little precipitation now have more than they did in 1901-1930. Also, in the period between 1931-1960, the west had a drought and since then it has moved westward towards the Arizona/Southern California area. It went from sparse precipitation in the west (1901-1930), to little precipitation nationwide (1931-1990), to heavier precipitation in the north and east.  One thing I wonder is if this was due to climate change or if it was just the course of weather patterns.

raw_comment:
Title: I know you've been busy in the last few years but did know how busy precipitation has been?

I notice that in 1931-1960 the blue spots are mostly where the yellow spots were in 1901-1930 and the yellow spots in 1930-1960 are mostly where the the blue spots are on 1901-1930.
In 1951-1990 the amount of blue has grown significantly but then looks like nothing when you look over at 1991-2020. 

I wonder if the blue means more or less precipitation. 
I also wonder why it has changed so much. My guess is global warming.

raw_comment:
On this graph, I notice many things. 

First of all, I noticed that there was a lot of rain in the west from 1901-1930, from there, in 1931-1960 it looks as if the west later went into a bit of a drought. This was likely due to the Dust Bowl, which happened throughout the 1930's.

Next, it looks like, from 1961-1990 the rain started to even out more and more. Then, from 1991-2020, the northeast was pummeled by rain. 

Overall, it looks as if the rain itself was pretty evenly distributed throughout the country. 

------------
I wonder why water is the most common trend.
------------
Finally, for the title of the graph, a good one may be:

Precipitation Across The Country Over Time

raw_comment:
The average amount of precipitation in the air has been going up. This is probably due to climate change. The east has been getting more rain and precipitation, which may mean that the East sends more co2 into the air then the rest of the country. In 1901 to 1930, the west used the be the wetlands/get the most rain. But because of what we have done with machines, and everything that adds to climate change, it has completely flipped what used to be natural. To being very unnatural wetlands that are seemingly unpredictable. 

I wonder if this will ever go back to normal. If we can get the precipitation levels in the US back to what it was in the early 1900's I think that would be a massive success. I wonder how much of this graph is because of climate change, and how much of it is natural. I believe that most of it is because of how we pollute the air.

This relates to me and my community because I live in the East. This is where the precipitation levels are the highest, and that is because we hurt the air more than the rest of the country. If the precipitation levels get to high, it could be bad for our environment and maybe even our safety.

1) What do you notice? 

I notice that precipitation net increased over the course of the century, especially in the East and the Midwest. However, there was more rainfall in Southwestern states in 1901 than in 2020, generally. 

2) What do you wonder? 

I wonder why there's generally more rainfall in most of America over the course of the century, as temperatures are hotter now. Even non-coastal areas in the East and the Midwest have more rainfall, which proves that not just the coastal areas are positively affected. Natural disasters, such as hurricanes and cyclones, could play a part in these graphs. I also wonder if the Southwestern drought plays some part in their limited rainfall. 

3) How does this relate to you and your community? 

I live in New York, and it seems as though we're getting much more rainfall!

What do you notice?
I notice that the precipitation in the North and Middle east have significantly risen in the last 30 years, while in the southwest, specifically Arizona, the land has gotten much dryer. During the other periods most of the precipitation varied a little although between 1931-1961 the mid-west was extremely arid. 

What do you wonder?
I wonder if that arid period between 1931-1961 was related to the dust bowl. I also wonder how global warming has affected the maps, because I believe it will continue making precipitation and weather more inconsistent.

How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me because as a member of the youth I have to take ownership of our future and as we see the adverse affects of climate change are already changing.

raw_comment:
The precipitation levels have significantly risen over the past century. These levels have particularly increased on the east coast, around the New England area of the United States. The southwest is also currently experiencing much less participation than it did in the first half of the 20th century. 
How could the west and the east of the United States be impacted so differently in such a short period of time? How has human activity created such a drastic and fast impact on the earth and climate?
Climate change and specifically precipitation levels have huge impacts on communities around the world. In Portland Maine, we hardly feel the effects of climate change compared to other areas around the U.S. Although, we have experienced much hotter summers, and warmer winters as well. The snow this winter barely lasted and would melt quickly after snow fall.  In many communities increased or decreased precipitation has an incredible impact on agriculture and soil. This not only affects farms that grow produce for human consumption, but also the animals that depend on vegetation for their food supply.

In that graph, it seemed the most precipitation occurred in the midwest, south, and northeast.

4.)The thing that is happening in the graphs is climate change and how is affecting our precipitation throughout the US. A good headline for the graph could be Climate Change VS Precipitation

raw_comment:
Thanks to all of the students who responded.   Here are some of the catchy headlines that we did receive: 

“Where Time Is Ticking and Precipitation Is Hitting” by Tal of New York
“Without Hesitation, There Is Cause for Worry about Precipitation” by Kenyan of Mesa, Arizona
"Is America's Rain Faucet Broken?" by Delali of Atlanta
"Precipitation Levels: Can You Predict the Future?" by Carlie of Chico, CA
“Water Is Life, But Will the Excess of Precipitation Become a Threat to the US?” by Nat of CELA in Jalisco, Mexico
"Skies Above! Precipitation in America Over the Years" by Tessa of Andover, MA

You can continue to post responses.  Please check back by Friday, September 24 to see the Reveal with a link to the original New York Times article, some questions about the graph, and a Stat Nugget.

View our archives that link to all past releases, organized by topic (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTopicIndex), 
graph type (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTypeIndex) and 
Stat Nugget (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsStatNuggetsIndex). 

Signing off – Sharon Hessney of Boston, where it now feels somewhat tropical with more frequent rain including the 5 inches of rain in one night from Hurricane Ida, and Chris Adkisson of Somerset, Kentucky, who had to cancel tennis practice yet again today.

raw_comment:
Headline: Precipitation Takes Over In the United States 

I noticed that the participation increased after 30 years in some areas but also decreased in others. I find this interesting because the areas that look like they increased in 2020 are along the coast meaning the oceans could be getting warmer leading to more evaporation along the coast. In the years 1931-1960 the dust bowl took over much of the west leaving states in extreme drought around 80 years later it looks like the perception has flipped, leaving the US with high amounts of rainfall
What is this change due to? A lot of scientists refer to climate change as a major problem in our world due to the carbon dioxide breaking down the ozone layer and I am wondering how much has to do with climate change and how much has to do with other factors. This relates to my community because over this summer we experienced weeks of rain, it was mid July and there were rainfall records broken. I think change is bound to happen but this graph shows it over a drastic scale of time.

raw_comment:

When considering the dust bowl, it makes sense that there would be such a tragic event (that was caused due to lack of precipitation) when there was statistically less precipitation.
I wonder if the increase in precipitation is due to the increased pollution from 1991 and 2020. 
This relates to my community because on the map, New Jersey is one of the places in the country with the most precipitation.

raw_comment: In these four graphs, you can see the incredible difference in precipitation over the years 1901-2021. During the early and mid-1900s, the precipitation levels were very different throughout the country. The US was booming with new industries and machines that had a big impact on the climate and precipitation. I also noticed that in the 1930s to 1960s there was a huge drought in the West and that was because in the 1930s the Dust Bowl took place. The Dust Bowl was an awful drought that hit the southern plains region and it lasted for almost a decade so that had a huge effect on the climate and the precipitation levels. In the 1960s to 1990s, there was a huge increase in precipitation and I wonder why there was such a big increase because the previous sixty years before some regions did not nearly experience that much rain. My thoughts are that the climate started to warm up and that caused a lot more precipitation. During the last thirty years, there has been a huge increase in rain and that is most likely because climate change has taken a huge toll on the earth all around. What I have noticed is that through the 20th century to the 21st century, the precipitation levels have been very different in all regions of the US. This relates to my community in many ways but mostly because we have been receiving a lot of rain in recent years. A catchy headline is “Precipitation and How it has Changed Over the Twentieth Century and Twenty-First Century”.

raw_comment: The first thing I noticed is that the precipitation levels are higher in the West during the 1901-1990 period. As time goes and the years pass by precipitation levels in the west start to decrease as the east starts to increase precipitation levels. In the years, 1931-1960, however, there seems to be little to no precipitation. This reminds me of the Dust Bowl in 1930 when the southwest suffered a severe drought. I wonder why over the years the location and amount or precipitation have varied. This could be because of climate change or pollution in the atmosphere. In the years 1991-2020, almost the entire east and part of the western part of the United States experiences 9+ inches of precipitation. I think this graph is to show people the changes over the years of precipitation levels across the country and maybe to prove a point. A good headline for this graph could be "Precipitation Changes in the US from 1901-2020".

raw_comment:
From 1991-2020 there is lots of precipitation up north and in the middle. There are also dry spots in the south western area so I wonder how the lack of precipitation affects them since their area isn't very blue. When I think of lack of rain I think of crops. Many farmers as of 2019, haven't been successful with their crops and some blame climate change. Climate change can affect the intensity and frequency of precipitation. In areas where precipitation is abundant, I wonder how it effects their daily lives. Thinking more urban, are cities and homes being flooded? Is transportation affected in these cities? In my area, we always have flash floods, people who play outdoor sports for schools practices are canceled. Atlanta being one of the cities that has a high employment rate, many people come here. We also have one of the busiest airports and many flights are canceled because of the dangerous weather. 

"Precipitation in the states and their affects on peoples daily lives"

We noticed that precipitation has gone up except for 1931-1960. Finally, we noticed that the precipitation has moved from west to east.

This impacts us and our community because the state we live in has had increased precipitation over the years. 

Our headline for the graph is, How Climate Change has Stirred the Weather Cycle

My Headline : Climate Change ; Do you believe us now?
What's going on?
These graphs depict how climate change is heavily effecting precipitation in the US. I also noticed how in 1901-1930 the precipitation and dry spots were more spread out and not as severe while going up through the years the dry spells are darker (meaning more severe) as well as the more wet spots are much darker. Seeing a visual representation of the climate through graphs makes the entire situation a lot more comprehensible. 
What do I onder?
I wonder when we will start taking meaningful and steady steps toward fixing the problem the little band aids ill not fix anything in the long run. 
How does it affect my community?
It affects our futures through what e can do for work and where we can live. Because climate change is such a huge problem and their aren't enough people taking steps to fix it the task will one hundred percent fall onto our shoulder and will burden us and our children more and more every passing day. 
Conclusion : Our world is not getting better and these graphs very clearly portray that. At this point there is no point in denying it when the proof is visibly in front of you. Our past generations have failed us even if they refuse to admit it. Everything is not okay, the orld is dying and we are not doing enough.

raw_comment:
What do I notice?
I notice that a specific pattern does not take place in this graph. In  1931-1960, we saw very scarce precipitation out West. We also saw heavy rainfall in 1991-2021 on the East Coast. The graph shows a significant change with no pattern. 

What do I wonder?
I wonder why the graph changes so often? Does this have something to do with the amount of pollution in the world today? In what ways have we changed our artificial area, and how may that affect this graph?

How does this relate to you and your community?
It allows me to look into the future and see what conditions the end may see. Will my children and their children face droughts or precipitation? It helps to predict the future.

raw_comment:
I notice that in general over time the average precipitation in the United States has increased. From 1901-1930 the highest increase in average precipitation was in the midwest. From 1931-1960 precipitation in the midwest decreased,  and precipitation increased along the coasts. From 1961-1990 precipitation increased by 3% in the majority of the country. From 1991-2020 precipitation increased by 6-9% in the eastern half of the country, but in the southwest it decreased by up to 9%.

I wonder if the dramatic change in precipitation is caused by global climate change. I wonder if the areas with significantly decreased precipitation were in drought. I also wonder how the change in amount of precipitation affected the ecosystems of the different regions.

This impacts me and my community because I live in the United States. This summer we had a lot more rain than usual where I live, so I have experienced this change in amount of precipitation and it matches the graph.

“How Precipitation Has Changed From 1901 to 2020”

4. The amount of precipitation across most of the U.S. has greatly increased overall. 

"The U.S. is Receiving the Most Rainfall Ever!"

What did I notice?
The difference between 1931-1960 and 1991-2020 is massive. In the eastern/northern region, there was pretty much no precipitation from 1931-1960. In 1991, we see a huge up-rise on the precipitation that was never there before. Even from 1961-1990 there wasn't very much precipitation there either. I also noticed that near New Mexico and Arizona, the precipitation switches around in every graph, from 1901-1930 and 1961-1990, there is a fair amount of precipitation. In the other two graphs, it's extremely dry. Why does it keep switching around every 30 years?
How does this relate to you and your community?
This relates to me because the weather in Georgia is getting more drastic. Every year the storms get worse, the summers get hotter, and the droughts last longer.

raw_comment:
If you look at the four graphs all in chronological order, you can see how much rain increases from 1901 to 2020. But it doesn't start and stay in the same place. 1901 and the turn of the century observed lots of industrial demand, leaving more and more smoke and soot in the atmosphere all over the country. In this period the dust storms along with the Great Depression also occurred which once again reduced the amount of rain. In the 1940s, the West Coast seems to get drier while the midwest and east coast seems to receive more rain. However, it seems to even out between 1961-1990, but the southwest gets extremely dry from 1991 until now. 

These graphs make me wonder how much industrialization and globalization has influenced weather patterns. I would think that using more and more natural resources would cause drier weather patterns, so I wonder what caused such a major shift. 

This affects my community because I live in an area that floods easily, making just 3 inches of rain a concern.

raw_comment:
Welcome to Wednesday's line moderation of “What’s Going On in This Graph?”  

Today’s graphs, which are displayed as maps called choropleths, show the percentage change in average U.S. precipitation for three 30-year periods .  The data for these graphs are collected from over 15,000 weather stations around the country, including more than 8,000 stations operated by volunteers.  Volunteers have gathered data since 1890.  This is one of the oldest and largest citizen-science projects anywhere.

From 9 am – 2 pm E.T. today, share with us your responses online to these questions -- "What do you notice?",  "What do you wonder?", and “How does this relate to you and your community?”  Plus, please share with us a catchy headline that captures the ideas in this graph. 

By Friday morning, we’ll reveal the free link to the article that included these graphs and much more.  We look forward to reading your discoveries.

Note that you can get a link to your response to share with your teacher and classmates by clicking the response box below your response “Email me when my comment is published.”  

View our archives with free link: organized by topic (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTopicIndex), 
graph type (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTypeIndex) and 
Stat Nugget (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsStatNuggetsIndex).  

The next “What’s Going On In This Graph?” will be released by Friday, Sept. 24 with moderation on Wednesday, Sept. 29.  The topic:  2020 Census and state redistricting.  Keep noticing and wondering!

image_description:
**1. Chart type**  
- **Faceted choropleth map** (four U.S. maps showing spatially encoded values with a diverging color scale)

**2. Layout techniques**  
- Uses **small multiples / faceting** in a **2×2 grid**
- Each panel represents a different **30-year period**
- No stacking

**3. Data variables**

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Geographic location (U.S. area/region) | Spatial/geographic | Position on map |
| 30-year period (1901–1930, 1931–1960, 1961–1990, 1991–2020) | Temporal | Faceting into separate map panels; panel title; small timeline marker above each panel |
| Precipitation compared with 20th century average | Quantitative | Color/hue on map (diverging brown-to-teal scale); legend |
| State name/abbreviation | Categorical/nominal | Text labels on map |

Then if we go to 1961 -1990 precipitation and droughts seem to be like balanced. Last from 1991 to 2020 Precipitation increased dramatically. I wonder that in 10 years precipitation will be more present in states located in the south. This relates a lot to my community because ten year ago precipitation was just presented in summer, but now it's still raining and we're about to face atumn. And I think that one of the main reasons could be global warming that is provoking climate change.

I can notice that there is a big difference in Iowa, that went from being not so dry, then very dry and then with a very high precipitation level. And in contrast, we can notice that Arizona was one of the states with highest precipitation levels in 1901-1930, and then in 1991-2020 became the State with more draught. 

I wonder if the north-east states of the United States will continue to have a higher precipitation levels in the future. I also have thoughts on whether Arizona is going to suffer lots of negative impacts due to draught and hot climate, for example, a lot of energy waste because of all the AC's that are probably going to be on daily use. Which means, there is probably going to be a rise in taxes causing more problems for people that don't have great jobs.

" Too little to too much, this is how precipitation changed in the US ".

Some things that stood out to me about these graphs were the difference in precipitation over the years and how it moves around the country. Seeing that the rain moved from being in the mid-western area to overall to the eastern area, showing that the southern-west area hasn't seen most change over the  years until 1901 and eastern side changing into a more dry weather.

I think the impact this has on my community is very eye opening, seeing the years pass by and seeing areas in California not having as much rain every year but seeing an increase in rain in the other side of the country is very shocking to me how much weather can change really quick in one location. Seeing southern California and Arizona being filled with rain in1901-1930 to now being one of the hottest areas currently is very eye opening.
My catchy headline to capture the main ideas of these graphs is "Watch as we collect information on one of the greatest changes in the U.S. History and what we can expect for the next couple years,"

Headline: Precipitation Takes Over In the United States 

I noticed that the participation increased after 30 years in some areas but also decreased in others. I find this interesting because the areas that look like they increased in 2020 are along the coast meaning the oceans could be getting warmer leading to more evaporation along the coast. In the years 1931-1960 the dust bowl took over much of the west leaving states in extreme drought around 80 years later it looks like the perception has flipped, leaving the US with high amounts of rainfall
What is this change due to? A lot of scientists refer to climate change as a major problem in our world due to the carbon dioxide breaking down the ozone layer and I am wondering how much has to do with climate change and how much has to do with other factors. This relates to my community because over this summer we experienced weeks of rain, it was mid July and there were rainfall records broken. I think change is bound to happen but this graph shows it over a drastic scale of time.

raw_comment:
What do you notice?

I noticed that the precipitation averaged in some of the U.S. in 1901-1930, then a little bit less than that in 1931-1960, then significantly more precipitation in 1961-1990, and then a lot more precipitation in 1991-2020. I also noticed that there was always a large part of California that was relatively dry compared to other states in all four of the 30-year periods. 

What do you wonder?

I wondered why the precipitation average has been increasing. Another thing that I wondered was why the east coast and the north seem to get more precipitation than the rest of the country. 

How does this relate to you and your community?

This relates to me and my community because my community seems to suffer from a relatively high precipitation average and has been for more decades.
